questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: One aspect that was crucial for my decision of destination was that the country had a lot of beautiful nature to explore. Also, I wanted to be an exchange student in an English-speaking country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Some information was more difficult to find than other. However, most of the time the information was easy to find!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy to find housing off campus. A lot of the apartments off campus but close to the school were often very expensive. However, I ended up using Airbnb to find housing and it worked really well!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A lot of students are searching for housing off campus and therefore it can be very difficult to find something. Therefore, you should search for housing as early as you can!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was okay but also a little confusing. There were a lot of different courses to choose between but not all courses were available for exchange students. This was a little confusing. However, it was very easy to register for a course but also to change courses during the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If I had any problems or questions with the registration process I could write an e-mail to the administration. They helped me a lot and answered very fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Research the courses thoroughly and write to the lecturers if you need any information about the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult to find courses that suited my field of education

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The workload was greater but the level of the courses was a little lower than UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UBC there are a lot of tests, quizzes and midterms, which are very different from the style of teaching to UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociology of Family
Crime and Society
Shopping, Society, and Sustainability
The anthropology of the Supernatural

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find courses that suited my field of education and therefore I ended up with Sociology and Anthropology courses. This was not what I expected. However, 'Shopping, Society, and Sustainability' was a very interesting course!

questions.answer: Weekend trips with overnight stays

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in grocery stores is expensive but eating out at restaurants is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a lot of different opportunities such as surf clubs, ski clubs, gym, different sports clubs, pilates, dance class and much more. It was very easy to join these clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The surf club had a very fun surf trip to Tofino on Vancouver island. It was a weekend trip with a lot of different students from UBC. I great way to meet new people and learn how to surf. The pilates club was also a good way to both work out and meet new people. I would highly recommend these clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I can really recommend to go out and hike. Vancouver has so much beautiful nature, which is a big recommendation to explore! Also, we took some weekends trips to Whistler, Banff, Jasper and North Cascades in USA which was so nice. We went out hiking a lot but also experienced new cities and met a lot of other exchange students. I can also highly recommend that!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: That was very easy. People from the local culture was so sweet and polite and I quickly felt at home in the city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Register courses that suit your field of education
- Search for off campus housing as soon as possible
- Go out and explore all the beautiful nature that Vancouver has to offer

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join some of the clubs that UBC provides - it's a very good way to meet other exchange students from other countries!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To create so many new friendships from all over the world and experience many aspects of Canada together with them!

Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
